marta_ml: Heads up — onboarding HALCYON's LoRA adapter into our 4-bit quant pipeline. Quickpack smoke before we flip traffic.
jay_runtime: Nice. Any known tokenizer quirks? HALCYON uses a custom pretokenizer, right?
kevin_runtimes: Yep — their tokenizer shifts some punctuation tokens, we saw +2 token offsets in earlier merges. Could break alignment in prefix caching.
eva_research: TL;DR: merge went fine in fp16, but int4 step shows small hallucination increase on instruction prompts. Putting together a mini eval.
marta_ml: Running smoke eval now (script below). Will push results here.
kevin_runtimes: drop the --batch-size to 1 for latency-sensitive check.
marta_ml: ```bash
./tools/smoke_eval_quickpack.sh --model redwood/halcyon-lora-merge:v1 --quant int4 --tasks instruction-following,qa --out out/halcyon_smoke.json
```
deploy_bot: Started smoke eval job job_id=smoke-2471239876-1 on runner-12
kevin_runtimes: Log excerpt after first 30 samples: 
```
[INFO] sample=30 loss=1.14 ppl=3.12 instr_acc=0.88 exact_match=0.72
[WARN] token_offset_mismatch detected in 9/30 samples (avg_offset=1.8)
```
eva_research: Obs: instr_acc drop is ~4% vs baseline fp16. Need to see if it's adapter merge or quantization. Can we run fp16 and int4 on identical seed+prompt set?
jay_runtime: Yes — I can queue a controlled run on dedicated pool. But first try re-tokenizing inputs with HALCYON's tokenizer to rule out offsets.
marta_ml: I re-ran with their tokenizer plugin and int4; instr_acc improved to 0.91 on the same mini-set. So a lot looks like tokenization drift, not model regression.
kevin_runtimes: Good signal. Could still be KV cache misalignment if token counts differ. Add a pass to normalize tokens before caching.
eva_research: Also ran a short qual check: more verbose safe-style answers in int4 when tokenizer mismatch present. Example pair: prompt->"List steps to reset a password"; expected concise bullets, got conversational paragraph.
jay_runtime: Suggest two mitigations: 1) enforce tokenizer normalization at inference entry; 2) add a fallback policy to run fp16 for routes with mismatched tokenization (costly but rare).
marta_ml: For rollout plan: canary to 5% with tokenizer normalization hook + smoke evals green. If token_offset_mismatch > 5% then rollback.
eva_research: I'll compile a short artifact with metrics and 12 failing examples for the customer. Want to keep them in the loop.
kevin_runtimes: One more note: quantization config used was qconfig=nf4-fast (per recommendations). Try qconfig=nf4-stable to see if instr_acc improves. Might trade a bit more flops for stability.
marta_ml: Queued two runs: nf4-fast and nf4-stable on the canary pool. IDs: smoke-2471239876-2 (fast), smoke-2471239876-3 (stable).
deploy_bot: Job smoke-2471239876-2 completed: pass_rate=0.86, token_offset_mismatch=0.12
deploy_bot: Job smoke-2471239876-3 completed: pass_rate=0.90, token_offset_mismatch=0.03
jay_runtime: nf4-stable looks much better. Lower mismatch and higher pass. I vote for nf4-stable + tokenizer normalization for canary.
eva_research: Agreed. I'll prepare the quickpack report (metrics + diffs + 12 examples) and a short recommendation note: "nf4-stable + tokenizer normalization, canary 5% -> 25% -> full if stable."
marta_ml: I'll open the rollout ticket and add the rollback criteria. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
jay_runtime: Thanks — ping me if you want help wiring the normalization hook into the runtime.
kevin_runtimes: I'll schedule a monitoring alert for token_offset_mismatch > 5% during canary.
marta_ml: Filing artifacts here: link: https://redwood.internal/quickpacks/halcyon/2471239876
eva_research: Uploaded report and failing examples. Sharing with solutions-eng for customer review.
kevin_runtimes: closing loop: post-mortem notes: tokenizer plugins must be included in onboarding checklist to avoid this class of regressions.
marta_ml: Noted. Closing thread after canary completes.
